# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95
Labels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api

## Why

The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.

`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads "no errors" while the caller sees rejections.

Recorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.

## What to do

Call `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged
- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`
- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass

## Tech notes

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

Out of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).

# Definition of Done

> The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a response body rejected directly by an HTTP client — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.

**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists. `createChatOrchestrator` returns an orchestrator whose `processMessage` and `processMessageStream` invoke the installed `OrchestratorHooks`. A test can drive `processMessage` with a provider that throws a string or a plain object and observe that `onError` is bypassed today because of the `error instanceof Error` gate in the `catch` block.

## Done when these pass

- [x] **calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing** — when a turn rejects with a string (`'string boom'`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance whose `message` is `'string boom'`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).
      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object** — when a turn rejects with a plain object (`{code: 503, detail: 'upstream down'}`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance carrying a non-empty `message`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).
      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [x] In `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`, coerce a caught non-`Error` rejection to an `Error` with a readable `message` (while passing an `Error` instance through unchanged) so `hooks.onError` always fires on any rejection inside the `try` block.
- [x] Confirm existing `Error`-instance tests in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` (`called with session and error when stream fails`, `error still propagates after onError hook`, `error path calls onError then afterSession`) remain green without modification.
- [x] Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` describing the behaviour change for existing consumers.

## Out of scope

- `beforeSession` escaping the `try` block (resolved separately in HALEngine#94).
- Usage accounting across tool rounds (resolved separately in HALEngine#93).
- Widening the `onError` hook parameter type away from `Error` (the ticket keeps `(session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>`).

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index eab0af2..044ff47 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -18,6 +18,8 @@ package, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.
 
 ### Changed
 
+- `onError` now fires for every rejection inside a turn, not only for `Error` instances. A thrown string, plain object or `undefined` previously skipped the hook while still reaching the caller, so a failure counter read zero for exactly those failures. An `Error` reaches the hook as the same instance; anything else is wrapped in a new `Error` with the raw value as its `cause`. The value rethrown to the caller is unchanged. If your hook assumed it only ran for `Error` rejections, expect it to run more often.
+
 - Every `SessionStore` member is now `Awaitable<T>` (`T | Promise<T>`) rather than a bare `T`, so a store backed by a database is expressible for the first time. `Awaitable` is exported from the package root. **A synchronous implementation needs no change** — `T` is assignable to `T | Promise<T>` in a return position — and `InMemorySessionStore` is unedited. The WebSocket connection handler now awaits `create` and the release that follows a close: it pauses the socket across the await so a frame sent before `connected` arrives is buffered rather than dropped, attaches its `close` listener before the await so a socket that closes mid-create leaves no session behind, and catches a rejection from either call so one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process with an unhandled rejection. **Migration note**: the `connected` frame now arrives one tick later, after the awaited `create`, so a client that waits for it (as the protocol already requires) sees no difference; only code that assumed the frame was emitted synchronously with the upgrade does.
 - **The engine no longer erases a conversation when its socket closes.** The WebSocket close handler called `sessionStore.delete(sessionId)` unconditionally, which meant that behind a durable store every conversation was written and then destroyed the moment the customer closed their tab — the opposite of what this engine's own documentation promised. `SessionStore.delete` now has no engine-internal caller at all and is purely your erasure primitive. The credentials the socket carried are cleared from the session on close, since they were issued for a request that is over; the entries are untouched. **Migration note**: to restore the old behaviour exactly, pass `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` — that one line is the whole migration. If you rely on the default store not growing, note that it is now bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours) rather than by the close handler; that is a memory bound, not a retention policy, and the retention decision remains yours.
 - The `afterModelResponse` hook now receives the accumulated usage across every provider call in the turn, not only the last one. Existing consumers that use this hook for billing or audit will see larger totals for turns that called tools — this is the correct number. A turn with no tool calls is unchanged.
diff --git a/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md b/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md
index 66ff9d3..e971b95 100644
--- a/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md
+++ b/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md
@@ -16,13 +16,8 @@
 - For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).
 - A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).
 - `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).
+- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)). The original value is preserved as the `cause` of the wrapping `Error`, including `undefined`, and the value rethrown to the caller is unchanged ([validated by: wraps a plain object rejection in an Error whose cause is that object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorCause.test.ts#L41), [validated by: wraps an undefined rejection in an Error whose cause is undefined and rethrows undefined](../../src/orchestration/onErrorCause.test.ts#L49)). An `Error` rejection reaches `onError` as the same instance ([validated by: passes an Error rejection to onError as the same instance](../../src/orchestration/onErrorCause.test.ts#L65)).
 
 ## Engine startup
 
 - The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).
-
-## Measured semantics — out of scope
-
-This property of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` is recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue does not change it; that is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.
-
-- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.
diff --git a/src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts b/src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts
index 8defbd2..c925054 100644
--- a/src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts
+++ b/src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts
@@ -147,8 +147,8 @@ export function createChatOrchestrator(
 
         if (hooks?.afterModelResponse) await hooks.afterModelResponse(session, responseText, totalUsage);
       } catch (error) {
-        if (hooks?.onError && error instanceof Error) {
-          await hooks.onError(session, error);
+        if (hooks?.onError) {
+          await hooks.onError(session, asError(error));
         }
         throw error;
       } finally {
@@ -343,3 +343,18 @@ async function saveSession(store: SessionStore | undefined, session: ChatSession
     log.error('orchestrator', 'session save failed', {sessionId: session.sessionId, error: message});
   }
 }
+
+// A hook typed against Error must see every rejection; the raw value stays reachable as `cause`.
+function asError(thrown: unknown): Error {
+  if (thrown instanceof Error) return thrown;
+  const message = typeof thrown === 'string' ? thrown : describeThrown(thrown);
+  return new Error(message, {cause: thrown});
+}
+
+function describeThrown(thrown: unknown): string {
+  try {
+    return JSON.stringify(thrown) ?? String(thrown);
+  } catch {
+    return String(thrown);
+  }
+}

@@ -18,6 +18,8 @@ package, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.
 
 ### Changed
 
+- `onError` now fires for every rejection inside a turn, not only for `Error` instances. A thrown string, plain object or `undefined` previously skipped the hook while still reaching the caller, so a failure counter read zero for exactly those failures. An `Error` reaches the hook as the same instance; anything else is wrapped in a new `Error` with the raw value as its `cause`. The value rethrown to the caller is unchanged. If your hook assumed it only ran for `Error` rejections, expect it to run more often.
+
 - Every `SessionStore` member is now `Awaitable<T>` (`T | Promise<T>`) rather than a bare `T`, so a store backed by a database is expressible for the first time. `Awaitable` is exported from the package root. **A synchronous implementation needs no change** — `T` is assignable to `T | Promise<T>` in a return position — and `InMemorySessionStore` is unedited. The WebSocket connection handler now awaits `create` and the release that follows a close: it pauses the socket across the await so a frame sent before `connected` arrives is buffered rather than dropped, attaches its `close` listener before the await so a socket that closes mid-create leaves no session behind, and catches a rejection from either call so one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process with an unhandled rejection. **Migration note**: the `connected` frame now arrives one tick later, after the awaited `create`, so a client that waits for it (as the protocol already requires) sees no difference; only code that assumed the frame was emitted synchronously with the upgrade does.
 - **The engine no longer erases a conversation when its socket closes.** The WebSocket close handler called `sessionStore.delete(sessionId)` unconditionally, which meant that behind a durable store every conversation was written and then destroyed the moment the customer closed their tab — the opposite of what this engine's own documentation promised. `SessionStore.delete` now has no engine-internal caller at all and is purely your erasure primitive. The credentials the socket carried are cleared from the session on close, since they were issued for a request that is over; the entries are untouched. **Migration note**: to restore the old behaviour exactly, pass `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` — that one line is the whole migration. If you rely on the default store not growing, note that it is now bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours) rather than by the close handler; that is a memory bound, not a retention policy, and the retention decision remains yours.
 - The `afterModelResponse` hook now receives the accumulated usage across every provider call in the turn, not only the last one. Existing consumers that use this hook for billing or audit will see larger totals for turns that called tools — this is the correct number. A turn with no tool calls is unchanged.

An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).

+- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).
